crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Resection Planning and Margins
children.blurb: Resection planning and margins covers the preoperative and intraoperative work of deciding how much tissue to remove around a tumor or lesion and how to confirm that the removed specimen has an adequate margin.

children.name: Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery
children.blurb: Haptic feedback in robotic surgery refers to the sensing and relay of force, vibration, and tissue resistance from surgical instruments back to the operating surgeon.

children.name: Virtual Surgical Rehearsal
children.blurb: Virtual surgical rehearsal uses patient-specific imaging and computational models to let a surgical team practice a planned procedure before entering the operating room.

children.name: Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery
children.blurb: Tremor stabilisation in microsurgery covers technologies that reduce or cancel physiological hand tremor during delicate procedures such as retinal, vascular, and neurosurgery.

children.name: Remote Telesurgery
children.blurb: Remote telesurgery is the practice of performing surgical procedures on a patient from a distance using robotic instruments, telecommunication links, and real-time imaging.

sections.body: Surgical robotics and navigation is the use of artificial intelligence to help a surgeon see, plan, and move inside the body with more precision than unaided hands and eyes allow. In current practice, AI is doing concrete work in image segmentation, instrument tracking, tissue classification, and control loops that steady a tool or align a preoperative scan with the live operative field. Resection planning uses patient imaging to suggest boundaries around a tumour or lesion, though the surgeon still decides what to remove. Haptic feedback systems try to translate force and texture into signals a surgeon can feel through a console, and virtual rehearsal builds patient-specific simulations for practice before an operation. Tremor stabilisation filters involuntary hand motion in microsurgery, while remote telesurgery lets a surgeon operate from a distance over a network. These are assistive technologies, not autonomous surgeons, and every one of them depends on clean data, reliable hardware, and a trained human in the loop.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work stands unevenly. Tremor filtering and master-slave teleoperation are mature in many commercial systems, and image-based navigation is routine in some specialties, but full autonomy is not solved and is not close. Haptic feedback remains difficult because force sensing at the tool tip, latency, and the cost of sterilizable hardware all limit what can be delivered. Virtual rehearsal is often preoperative and approximate, not a validated predictor of every intraoperative event. Telesurgery is constrained by network latency, bandwidth, and the need for a local surgical team if the connection fails. The site tracks 1000 medical AI models, and surgical robotics is a small, hardware-bound part of that count, which reflects how much of the field still depends on physical devices and operating room integration. The site also tracks 6 active product liability and wrongful death lawsuits against AI companies, a reminder that clinical deployment carries legal exposure when systems fail or are misused.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Resection Planning and Margins is the place to start for how AI turns scans into suggested cut lines and how margin status is checked after removal. Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery explains the sensing and actuation problem, why force feedback is hard to deliver through a console, and what current systems can and cannot convey. Virtual Surgical Rehearsal covers patient-specific simulation, the data it needs, and the gap between rehearsal and real tissue behaviour. Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery focuses on filtering and compensation at small scales, where millimetre errors matter and control loops must be fast. Remote Telesurgery looks at networked operation, latency budgets, fallback plans, and the regulatory questions that follow a surgeon who is not in the room. Together these pages move from planning to sensing to simulation to micro-scale control to remote execution, which is the practical arc of AI in surgical robotics and navigation.
